articles.headline: Indra Buys As Pontes Factory for 18 Million Euro Military Vehicle Plant
articles.subtitle: The Spanish defence giant will manufacture amphibious combat vehicles, bridge-launching systems and wheeled artillery at a 15,000-square-metre site in Penapurreira, creating 70 to 120 direct jobs
articles.body: Indra, the Spanish defence and technology multinational, has completed the purchase of the former Hierros Añón factory in the Penapurreira industrial estate in As Pontes, investing 18 million euros to establish a military vehicle manufacturing plant. The 15,000-square-metre facility sits on a 50,000-square-metre plot and will produce amphibious combat vehicles, bridge-launching systems and wheeled artillery for the Spanish Armed Forces. Indra will take possession in September and expects to begin production before the end of the year after minor adaptations. The company forecasts 70 to 120 direct highly skilled jobs plus numerous indirect positions in the supply chain. The arrival of Indra has already had a knock-on effect: a 1.6 million euro contract with Arteixo Telecom, a neighbouring factory in the same estate, will reduce the impact of a temporary layoff plan affecting 78 workers. As Pontes mayor Valentín González Formoso described Indra as a technology and defence industry giant that will create a manufacturing hub benefiting the whole area. The site was previously occupied by Chinese company Daxiong, whose project failed within three years.

articles.headline: Monforte's New Ornamental Fountain Draws Residents Back to Os Condes Park
articles.subtitle: A 25-metre-diameter circular fountain with light effects has reopened the park after construction, bringing back the daily tertulias of retired neighbours who had relocated during the works
articles.body: The new ornamental fountain in Monforte de Lemos's Parque de Os Condes has been inaugurated, drawing the park's regulars back to their traditional benches after months of displacement during construction. The fountain measures 25 metres in diameter and features illuminated water jets that operate from 11:00 to 15:00 and 18:00 to 02:00 daily. During the works, the retired residents who gather daily for tertulias had relocated across the street to the Ponte Fontecha area near the statue of poet Manuel María. With the fountain complete, they have returned, and the new centrepiece dominates conversation. Opinions are mixed: some residents praise the improved paving and aesthetics, while others criticise the lack of shade from trees that were removed and question whether a fountain of this size was needed given the proximity of other water features. The fountain suffered an attempted sabotage the night before its inauguration, when hooded individuals were caught on camera pouring green dish soap into the water, apparently hoping to generate foam. The council brought in an anti-foam treatment from a specialist company in O Porriño.

articles.headline: Father Reports Assault on Son at Sarria Summer Camp to Civil Guard
articles.subtitle: A nine-year-old boy was allegedly kicked, scratched and had his hair pulled by four other children at the Aventura no Camiño camp. The council says monitors did not witness the incident and will speak to all parties
articles.body: A father has filed a complaint with the Guardia Civil alleging that his nine-year-old son was assaulted by four other children at the Aventura no Camiño summer camp organised by the Concello de Sarria. According to the denuncia, when the father arrived to collect his son on Friday at around 13:30, he found the boy crying. The child said he had been kicked, had his hair pulled, was scratched and had nails dug into him by four other participants, two aged around 14 or 15 and two closer to his own age. The father said he asked the camp monitors for an explanation and was told the perpetrators had already been punished and that it had not been serious. A health centre examination recorded abrasions on the boy's neck. The camp organiser said the monitors did not witness the alleged assault, which reportedly occurred in the bathroom area where monitors are not present, and that the children had been playing together without previous problems. The council said it will speak to all parties and that a repeat incident would lead to expulsion. The father said he will go to the town hall on Monday to pursue the matter further.

articles.headline: Lugo Councillors Cut Summer Holidays Short Ahead of 2027 Municipal Elections
articles.subtitle: The motion of censure that brought Elena Candia to the mayoralty and the proximity of the 2027 vote have compressed the political calendar, with most of the corporation taking minimal or no August break
articles.body: Most members of the Lugo municipal corporation will take minimal or no summer holidays this year, according to El Progreso, as the political calendar compresses under the weight of the recent motion of censure and the approaching 2027 local elections. Mayor Elena Candia, who took office in May after the Partido Popular ousted the previous administration, will combine rest with attention to council business, including short trips to the A Mariña beaches. Culture councillor Javier Vázquez said this will be an atypical summer because of the San Froilán festivities and the cultural programme planned for September, adding that holidays will have to wait. Other councillors plan short breaks at Galician coastal destinations including O Grove, Raxó and A Mariña. The compressed schedule reflects the unusual situation of a new administration with limited time to deliver on its programme before facing the electoral test. The opposition is also expected to maintain a high level of activity through August as the campaign period effectively begins.

articles.headline: Ceuta Death Toll Rises to at Least 72 as Morocco Admits 11 Dead on Its Side
articles.subtitle: The Spanish government reports 72 confirmed deaths from the mass border crossing, while Ceuta's regional government counts 88. Morocco acknowledged 11 deaths on its territory and blamed misinterpretation of a Supreme Court ruling
articles.body: The death toll from the mass border crossing into Ceuta has risen to at least 72, the Spanish government confirmed on Sunday, as the improvised morgue at the military hospital continued to receive bodies. The Ceuta regional government puts the figure at 88. Morocco acknowledged for the first time that 11 people died on its territory during the incident, attributing the tragedy to misinterpretation of a Spanish Supreme Court ruling that tightened conditions for turning away migrants intercepted at sea. Morocco's government said the ruling had created confusion and that it had acted to restore order. Spain's Interior Ministry said more than 48,300 of the estimated 50,000 to 60,000 people who entered the enclave since Thursday had returned to Morocco. A 500-metre pneumatic floating barrier is being installed at the Tarajal breakwater, designed to stand 30 to 70 centimetres above the water. The measure responds to the Supreme Court ruling that migrants cannot be summarily returned unless they have bypassed a physical barrier. EU interior ministers are scheduled to meet by videoconference on Tuesday to address the crisis, which has exposed deep divisions within the bloc over migration policy.

articles.headline: Thirteen Killed as Tourist Plane Crashes Over Peru's Nazca Lines
articles.subtitle: A small aircraft operated by Aerodiana went down shortly after takeoff from Pisco, killing all 11 passengers and two crew members. Two of the victims were Spanish nationals, the Foreign Ministry confirmed
articles.body: Thirteen people died on Saturday when a tourist aircraft crashed while flying over the Nazca Lines in southern Peru, according to police commander Jorge Andrade. The plane, operated by Peruvian airline Aerodiana, had taken off from Pisco airport about 240 kilometres south of Lima and lost contact with the control tower minutes later. All 11 passengers and two crew members were killed, with no survivors. Four bodies had been recovered by Saturday evening as rescue teams worked among the wreckage. Spain's Foreign Ministry confirmed that two of the victims were Spanish nationals. The cause of the accident is under investigation by Peru's civil aviation authority. The Nazca Lines, a UNESCO World Heritage site consisting of enormous geoglyphs etched into the desert floor, are a major tourist attraction and flights over them are a common excursion. The area has seen previous aviation accidents, including a 2022 crash that killed seven people. The aircraft was a small propeller plane typical of the sightseeing flights that operate from Pisco and nearby Ica.

articles.headline: Trump Cancels Iran Strikes, Says Talks Will Resume Monday
articles.subtitle: The US president said allies including Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar asked him to hold off because they believe a deal on the Strait of Hormuz can be reached, after days of preparation for major energy infrastructure strikes
articles.body: Donald Trump said on Sunday that he has suspended planned military strikes against Iran and that negotiations will resume on Monday, in a significant de-escalation after days of preparation for major attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure. Speaking aboard Air Force One en route to Egypt, Trump said he had been in contact with the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, who asked him to cancel the strikes because they believe a deal can be reached on the Strait of Hormuz. The president had been weighing weekend military action against Iranian power plants, refineries and other energy infrastructure, according to sources who spoke to CBS News. The planned escalation followed weeks of tit-for-tat strikes that had drawn in multiple countries, including a drone attack on a US-owned LNG tanker at the Egyptian port of Damietta. Iran had warned it would respond to any strikes on its power plants by hitting energy infrastructure across the region. Trump's announcement represents the latest shift in a conflict that has oscillated between negotiation and military escalation since it began in February. The Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil passes, has been a central flashpoint throughout.

articles.headline: Three Killed in Bomb Attack at Moscow Restaurant, State Media Reports
articles.subtitle: Security officials said a woman attempted to enter the establishment with explosives but was stopped by a security guard, triggering the blast. The attack comes amid heightened security in the Russian capital
articles.body: Three people were killed after a bomb detonated at a restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media reported on Sunday. Security officials said a woman tried to enter the restaurant carrying explosives but was stopped by a security guard, at which point the device detonated. The attack occurred at an establishment in the Russian capital, though authorities did not immediately identify the venue or provide further details about the victims. No group claimed responsibility in the immediate aftermath. The bombing comes at a time of heightened security in Moscow, which has seen occasional attacks since the start of the war in Ukraine. Russian authorities have frequently blamed Ukrainian intelligence for attacks on Russian soil, though Kyiv typically denies involvement. The incident is under investigation by Russia's Federal Security Service. The attack follows a pattern of occasional violent incidents in Russian cities that authorities attribute to the conflict in Ukraine, though independent verification of official accounts is often limited.

articles.headline: July Set to Be Driest on Record for England and Wales After Relentless Heatwaves
articles.subtitle: Southern England received just 1 percent of its long-term average rainfall last month, with half of England and all of Wales now in drought. Firefighters responded to 393 wildfires in July, the busiest month on record
articles.body: July is set to be the driest month on record for England and Wales, according to the Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales, as four record-breaking heatwaves since May have left landscapes parched and fuelled hundreds of wildfires. Southern England received just 1 percent of its long-term average rainfall for July, while England as a whole received 7 percent. The Thames at Reading recorded its lowest ever level. Approximately 23 million people across England and Wales are under hosepipe bans, though water companies say record winter rainfall means reservoirs remain close to expected levels and drinking water supplies are not threatened. Firefighters responded to 393 wildfires across England and Wales in July, making it the busiest month on record and placing significant pressure on crews. Hundreds of people have been evacuated due to fire threats, compared with approximately 50 in all of 2025. The Met Office predicts that the climate crisis will make UK summers 1 to 6 degrees Celsius hotter and up to 60 percent drier by 2070 compared with 1990. Climate scientist Dr Chloe Brimicombe of the University of Oxford said the summer has been a compounding of dry weather leading to droughts, heatwaves and wildfires, and called for better long-term planning.

articles.headline: Five Dead, 41 Missing After Indonesia Ferry Catches Fire
articles.subtitle: The vessel carrying 271 people caught fire off Madura island in East Java. Rescue operations are ongoing and the cause of the blaze is under investigation
articles.body: At least five people have died and 41 are missing after a ferry carrying 271 passengers and crew caught fire off the coast of Madura island in East Java, Indonesia, authorities reported on Sunday. The vessel was travelling between Indonesian islands when the fire broke out. Rescue teams have been deployed to search for survivors, with the navy and local fishermen assisting in the operation. The cause of the fire is under investigation. Ferry accidents are relatively common in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands where ferries are a primary mode of transport. Safety standards on many vessels have been a longstanding concern, with overcrowding and inadequate safety equipment frequently cited as contributing factors in past incidents. The country has experienced several major ferry disasters in recent decades, including the sinking of the KM Sinar Bangun in 2018 which killed more than 160 people. The latest incident comes during the peak travel season, when many Indonesians are travelling between islands for holidays.

articles.headline: OpenAI's Internal Astra Model Solves 10 Long-Standing Open Math Problems
articles.subtitle: The unreleased model produced solutions to problems in high-dimensional geometry, coding theory and group theory that had seen no progress for at least a decade, at a cost of roughly $2,000 per problem in API tokens
articles.body: OpenAI announced on 1 August that an internal version of its next major model, codenamed Astra, has produced solutions to ten open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science that had seen no progress on the main result for at least a decade. The problems span high-dimensional geometry, coding theory, arithmetic circuit complexity, group theory, operator algebras, quantum complexity, lattice cryptography and extremal combinatorics. Among the results are new upper bounds on sphere-packing density, exponentially improved bounds on binary and spherical codes, a construction establishing the existence of non-sofic groups, and a disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture. The total token cost to find all ten solutions was roughly $2,000 at Sol API rates, according to OpenAI. The arguments were formalised in Lean 4 certificates and published alongside a paper and reasoning walkthroughs. The announcement follows Anthropic's recent disclosure that Claude Mythos had identified cryptographic weaknesses, and has prompted comparisons to Deep Blue's chess victory. Mathematician Kirwin Hampshire published an essay describing a profound spiritual crisis brought on by AI mathematical capability, while Terence Tao has described the shift toward big mathematics with large-scale human-AI collaboration.

articles.headline: Go 1.27 Released With Interactive Tour and Language Improvements
articles.subtitle: The latest version of the Go programming language introduces new features and refinements, with a community-built interactive tour highlighting the changes. The release has drawn significant attention on Hacker News
articles.body: Go 1.27 has been released, the latest version of Google's systems programming language, and has quickly become one of the most discussed topics on Hacker News with over 250 points and 100 comments. The release includes language improvements, performance enhancements and tooling updates. An interactive tour of the new features, built by the community and hosted by VictoriaMetrics, provides a hands-on walkthrough of the changes. Go has maintained a steady release cadence since its 1.0 release in 2012, with each version bringing incremental improvements while maintaining backward compatibility. The language has grown significantly in adoption, particularly in cloud infrastructure, networking and DevOps tooling, where its simplicity, fast compilation and built-in concurrency model are valued. The 1.27 release continues this trajectory with refinements to the compiler, runtime and standard library. The interactive tour format has been praised as an accessible way for developers to understand what is new without reading through lengthy release notes.

articles.headline: ByteDance Releases Seedance 2.5 for One-Take AI Video Generation
articles.subtitle: The updated model supports flexible referencing and single-take creation, generating 376 points on Hacker News. The release signals ByteDance's continued push into AI-generated video content
articles.body: ByteDance has released Seedance 2.5, an updated version of its AI video generation model that supports one-take creation and flexible referencing. The release generated 376 points and nearly 200 comments on Hacker News, reflecting strong interest in AI video generation capabilities. Seedance 2.5 allows users to generate video content from text prompts with improved coherence and temporal consistency compared to previous versions. The model represents ByteDance's continued investment in generative AI, building on the company's experience with large-scale recommendation systems and content platforms including TikTok and Douyin. AI video generation has become one of the most competitive areas in the AI industry, with companies including OpenAI, Google and Meta all developing or releasing video generation models. The quality and length of AI-generated video has improved dramatically over the past year, though challenges remain in maintaining consistency across longer clips and avoiding artifacts. ByteDance's release positions it alongside other major players in a rapidly evolving market where the ability to generate convincing video from text prompts could transform content creation workflows.

articles.headline: Uber Builds Autonomous Vehicle Empire With 30-Plus Partnerships
articles.subtitle: The ride-hailing giant has partnered with or invested in more than 30 autonomous vehicle companies over the past two years, taking a global approach after selling its own self-driving unit in 2020
articles.body: Uber has assembled a sprawling network of more than 30 autonomous vehicle partnerships and investments over the past two years, according to a TechCrunch analysis, marking a dramatic reversal from its 2020 decision to exit self-driving development. After selling its Advanced Technologies Group to Aurora and divesting other moonshots including Jump and Elevate, Uber has quietly rebuilt its autonomous vehicle strategy through partnerships rather than in-house development. The company has taken a global approach, working with autonomous vehicle developers across multiple continents and technology approaches. Partners include Aurora, in which Uber retains an equity stake, along with Waymo, Motional and numerous other companies developing self-driving technology for ride-hailing and delivery. The strategy allows Uber to offer autonomous ride-hailing in multiple markets without bearing the full cost of developing the technology itself. The approach mirrors Uber's asset-light model in its core business, where it connects drivers with passengers without owning vehicles. The company has also invested in autonomous delivery and freight, extending the model beyond passenger transport. The partnerships cover robotaxis, autonomous delivery vehicles and self-driving trucks.

articles.headline: OpenAI's Astra Model Solves Decade-Old Math Problems for $2,000 Each
articles.subtitle: An internal version of OpenAI's next major model produced solutions to ten open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, with results formalised in Lean 4 and published alongside reasoning walkthroughs
articles.body: OpenAI has revealed that an internal version of its next major model, Astra, produced solutions to ten open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science that had resisted progress for at least a decade. The results span high-dimensional geometry, coding theory, arithmetic circuit complexity, group theory, operator algebras, quantum complexity, lattice cryptography and extremal combinatorics. Each solution cost roughly $2,000 in API tokens, a fraction of what human-led research would require. The findings were formalised in Lean 4 certificates and published alongside a paper and reasoning walkthroughs. The announcement follows Anthropic's recent disclosure that Claude Mythos had identified cryptographic weaknesses in a post-quantum signature candidate, and together the two developments have intensified debate about AI's role in fundamental research. Simon Willison noted on his blog that the transparency was decent but that the prompts used remain unpublished. Mathematician Kirwin Hampshire published an essay describing a profound spiritual crisis brought on by AI mathematical capability, while Terence Tao has described the shift toward big mathematics with large-scale human-AI collaboration. The results were achieved by an internal model not yet released to the public, and OpenAI has not disclosed how many problems were attempted without reaching a solution.

articles.headline: EU AI Act Transparency Rules Take Effect Across Europe
articles.subtitle: From 2 August, providers and deployers of AI systems in the EU must label AI-generated content and disclose when users are interacting with a chatbot, marking the first major enforceable deadline of the landmark regulation
articles.body: The European Union's AI Act reached its first major enforceable milestone on 2 August 2026, as the transparency obligations under Article 50 came into full effect. The rules apply to any organisation that provides or deploys AI systems within the EU, regardless of where the company is based. Under the new rules, providers of generative AI systems must ensure that AI-generated content is identifiable through machine-readable markings. Deployers must clearly label deepfakes and any AI-generated text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest. Chatbots and other AI systems that interact with users must disclose that the user is interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the context. The European Commission published detailed guidelines on the transparency obligations in July 2026. The AI Office now has supervisory and fining authority over general-purpose AI model providers, with penalties of up to 15 million euros or 3 percent of global annual turnover. Wired reported that the new rules have led to concerns about disclosure fatigue, as Europeans will now encounter AI labels across many aspects of daily life. The high-risk AI system obligations have been deferred to December 2027 under the Digital Omnibus, but the transparency rules proceed on schedule. The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 with a phased implementation timeline.
